name: Cooking oils, other (canola, sunflower, coconut, avocado, sesame)

Cd.binding_scope: Fats, oils, and fat emulsions (water-in-oil type)

iAs.label: Inorganic arsenic is a component of total arsenic (iAs <= tAs). The iAs value (100 ug/kg) is not below the binding total arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), so inorganic arsenic is governed by and bounded by the total arsenic ceiling; no separate iAs ceiling is published. It is enforced by reflex speciation whenever tAs is elevated.

tHg.binding_scope: Fats, oils, and fat emulsions (water-in-oil type)

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury forms by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish; a pressed or extracted plant oil has no methylation pathway and no mercury source. No government sets a methylmercury limit for a culinary oil.

Ni.rationale: No sovereign maximum level exists for nickel in culinary oils or fats. Nickel can enter a fat as residual hydrogenation catalyst (Raney nickel) in any hardened or partially hydrogenated fraction; virgin and refined liquid oils are not hydrogenated. Because a real exposure pathway exists, the cell is held under a reflex screen rather than declared not-material.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on each lot; any hydrogenated or partially hydrogenated oil is monitored under ALARA against the tightest available food nickel context.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. Chromium is not lipophilic and does not partition into a refined lipid matrix. Total-chromium food MLs do exist for other matrices (for example HK Cap. 132V meat, vegetables, cereals, pulses and fish; dairy milk powder and liquid milk; gelatin/collagen and fishery products), but none is an oil or fat. Rebuttable and audited against the register each build.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS as a screen; reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel number for a food; it is the toxic species obtained by reflex speciation. Any lot whose total-chromium screen exceeds the reflex trigger is speciated, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: IC-ICP-MS Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) on any total-Cr exceedance.

Sn.rationale: Tin migrates into food only from tinplate cans; culinary oils are sold in glass, PET, or lined containers, not tinplate. No non-canned tin pathway exists for oils.

Al.rationale: No sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. Aluminium does not partition into a refined lipid matrix and a plant oil has no aluminium uptake or migration pathway. Aluminium food limits that exist elsewhere are not contaminant MLs reaching an oil: China's GB 2762 eliminated aluminium as a contaminant and aluminium in food is instead governed as a GB 2760 permitted additive under its ADI (finished-product residue caps such as baked foods 100000 and starch noodles/vermicelli 200000), and the AU-NZ aluminium limits are infant-formula-specific (Schedule 19 non-soy 500 / soy 1000). None is an edible oil. Rebuttable and audited against the register each build.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; face value, no reconstitution; read-across / control / not-material for unregulated cells; no occurrence percentiles)
lineage_note: Initial Cat-30 government-limit standard. Edible-oil MLs (EU 2023/915, Codex named-vegetable-oils, GSO 193:2021, Thailand MOPH 414, India FSSAI, Israel FCS) govern Pb/Cd/tAs/iAs/tHg at face value; nickel is held under a hydrogenation-catalyst screen (no sovereign oil Ni ML); Al/Sn/total-Cr not-material; Cr-VI reflex control; MeHg not-material (no marine methylation pathway in a plant oil).
